The cart stores a single `_discount` field, and applying a code overwrites it. After SAVE10 and then TAKE15 the total is 65.00. If both discounts stacked it would be 57.00 or 58.50, so the test tells the cases apart. It passed.

The expected 65.00 only holds if the second code replaces the first; stacking either way round gives a different total.

findings.title: Spec doesn't say whether to round the discount or the final total
findings.detail: total() applies ROUND_HALF_UP once, to the discounted total. Another reasonable reading rounds the discount amount first and then subtracts it. The two give different answers when the subtotal is 0.05 and the code is PercentOff(10): rounding the total gives 0.045 -> 0.05, while rounding the discount gives 0.005 -> 0.01 off, so 0.04. No scenario covers this.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a scenario that says which value is rounded: the discount or the total.

findings.title: Spec doesn't say what an unknown code does to a discount already applied
findings.detail: apply_code calls lookup before assigning, so an UnknownDiscountCode leaves the earlier discount in place. Another implementation could clear it instead. No scenario covers this.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a scenario for applying an unknown code to a cart that already has a discount.

findings.title: Spec doesn't say what happens when a code is registered twice
findings.detail: register silently replaces an existing code, including one that differs only in case ("save10" after "SAVE10"). Another implementation could reject the duplicate. No scenario covers this.

findings.title: A NaN percent or amount raises InvalidOperation, not ValueError
findings.detail: With PercentOff(Decimal('NaN')), the chained comparison raises decimal.InvalidOperation, which is not a ValueError, so this invalid discount isn't rejected with ValueError as the requirement says. A non-numeric string fails the same way, in the Decimal(str(...)) conversion. No scenario covers these inputs.
